sheet-1.description: The lower half of the first sheet of the 1928 Bloomingdale atlas, drawn at 50 feet to an inch below a heavy line that separates it from the key map, index, key and water and fire notes in the upper half. It covers the north bank of the Pequannock River at the western bend of the Paterson and Hamburg Turnpike, in the strip between Butler, across the river in Morris County, and the hillside to the north. Carmantown Road comes down the slope from the north-west, is met by Crane Avenue from the west, and turns east along the top of a steep bank; Old Road runs west from that corner, and Acton Place, a short lane given an arbitrary name, branches north from Carmantown Road. Woodward Avenue is marked as not open at the western edge. The Turnpike follows the foot of the bank between Carmantown Road and the river. The ground is mostly open and wooded, shown by heavy stippling, with scattered frame dwellings and outbuildings on large lots, a few concrete-block dwellings, hen houses at the eastern edge and an automobile repair shop on the river side of the Turnpike. The river and the county boundary along it fill the southern edge, with the note that the far bank is shown on the map of Butler. Lot numbers are arbitrary, as the index notes. The sheet has its own north point and scale of feet. The map adjoins sheet 5 at its western edge and the Turnpike north of Main Street, drawn on sheet 2, to the south-east.
notes: Carmantown Road is today Glenwild Avenue; its eastern stretch along the bank follows today's Glenwild Avenue towards the Turnpike.
Old Road is today Delazier Place.
Acton Place (arbitrary name) lies on or near today's Babcock Lane; not used as control because the drawn junction did not agree with the modern one.

Placed from two hand-picked junctions on Glenwild Avenue (Crane Avenue, Delazier Place) about 30 m apart, with the configured scale and a rotation of -33 degrees; the sheet's own north point suggests about -18 degrees and was not used. Low confidence away from Carmantown Road.

50 ft. Upper half is the key map (950 ft to an inch), index and water and fire notes (masked out); lower half is the map: Carmantown Road (now Glenwild Avenue), Crane Avenue, Acton Place (arbitrary), Old Road (now Delazier Place), Woodward Avenue (not open), Paterson and Hamburg Turnpike along the Pequannock River. Placed from two hand-picked junctions on Glenwild Avenue 30 m apart with the configured scale and a rotation of -33 degrees (derived point); low confidence.

sheet-2-1.description: The main part of sheet 2, at 50 feet to an inch, covering the centre of Bloomingdale on the north bank of the Pequannock River. Main Street runs across the lower part of the sheet from its junction with the Paterson and Hamburg Turnpike at the western edge, where a concrete bridge carries it over the river towards Butler, eastwards towards Valley View. This stretch is the commercial centre: stores, a post office, a bank, an ice cream parlour, hotel rooms, automobile repair shops, bowling alleys, the Bloomingdale Baptist Church and the Public Overall Co. works, with dwellings and outbuildings behind them reaching down to the river. North of Main Street a steep bank rises to the Bloomingdale Public School and a residential grid of Grove, Pearl and Valley View running north to Pleasant View Avenue, crossed by Captolene Avenue and, at the eastern edge, High Street. Most houses here are frame dwellings on regular lots, many of the blocks still largely empty. Kikeout Brook joins the Pequannock in the south-western corner and the county boundary between Passaic and Morris Counties follows the river. A heavy line in the upper-left corner cuts off the second part of the sheet, which shows the Turnpike north of Main Street; the small area marked 2 just inside that line at the Main Street junction is drawn in outline only and repeats that part. The sheet carries its own north point and scale of feet; house numbers are arbitrary.
notes: Grove, Pearl, Valley View and High are today Grove Street, Pearl Street, Valley View Avenue and High Street.
Captolene Avenue west of Grove is drawn running to the Turnpike at the heavy line; today it ends at Glenwild Avenue.
Pearl south of Captolene Avenue is drawn at a different angle from today's Pearl Street; a hand-picked point at High and Pearl was 7 m from the fit and was left out.
Seam with sheet 3 along Valley View: the line work steps by about 5 to 8 m.

50 ft. Two parts. Part 1 (main): Main Street from the Turnpike junction east, Grove, Pearl, Valley View, Captolene Avenue, High, Pleasant View Avenue; public school, Baptist church, post office, bank. Part 2 (upper left corner, behind a heavy line): the Paterson and Hamburg Turnpike north of Main Street with the Municipal and Fire Department building, drawn at the same scale and rotation but shifted up the page; placed by points carried from part 1 (the Main Street junction and the Club House, drawn on both).

sheet-2-2.description: The second part of sheet 2, drawn in the upper-left corner of the sheet behind a heavy line at the same scale, 50 feet to an inch, and the same orientation as the main part but shifted up the page to save space. It shows the Paterson and Hamburg Turnpike running north from its junction with Main Street in the centre of Bloomingdale, between the Pequannock River on the west and the rising ground on the east. At the junction Main Street turns south-west over a concrete bridge across the river towards Butler; water pipes are drawn in both streets. Along the west side of the Turnpike stand the Municipal and Fire Department building, a few frame dwellings and a club house on the corner of Main Street; the east side is open land. The river runs along the western edge with the county boundary between Bloomingdale in Passaic County and Butler in Morris County, and a note refers to the map of Butler for the far bank. House numbers are arbitrary. The junction and the club house also appear, in outline, in the corner of the main part of the sheet, which is how this part was placed.
notes: Placed from two points carried from part 1 of this sheet (the Main Street junction and a corner of the club house, drawn on both parts), with part 1's scale and rotation; low confidence at its northern end.
The Municipal and Fire Department building stands on the west side of the Turnpike north of Main Street.

Part 2 (upper left corner, behind a heavy line): the Paterson and Hamburg Turnpike north of Main Street with the Municipal and Fire Department building, drawn at the same scale and rotation but shifted up the page; placed by points carried from part 1 (the Main Street junction and the Club House, drawn on both).

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3, at 50 feet to an inch, covers the eastern half of central Bloomingdale on the north bank of the Pequannock River. Main Street crosses the sheet diagonally from the steep bank in the west to Ryerson Avenue in the south-east. North of it Reeve Avenue, Leary Avenue and Ryerson Avenue run up to Wanaque Road along the top of the sheet, forming two long residential blocks of frame dwellings with small outbuildings and many empty lots; Hennion Avenue leaves Ryerson Avenue at the eastern edge. In the west Valley View curves down from High Street towards Main Street along the top of a high bank, with a stretch marked not opened, and a corner box repeats Captolene Avenue and High from sheet 2. At Reeve Avenue and Main Street stands a group of brick and concrete garages with an automobile show room and repair shop, and further east the Methodist Protestant Church. South of Main Street the river divides around Sloan Park, an island reached by a wooden bridge, and the county boundary between Passaic and Morris Counties follows the main channel, beyond which the map of Butler takes over. Dwellings are mostly two-storey frame houses; house numbers are arbitrary. The sheet has its own north point and scale of feet.
notes: Wanaque Road is today Oak Street.
Hennion Avenue is today Henion Place.
Valley View is today Valley View Avenue; its curved stretch south of High is marked not opened.
The junction of Wanaque Road and Reeve Avenue was hand-picked at a position found by an earlier detector run.
Shared junction with sheet 4 at Wanaque Road and Ryerson Avenue placed about 6 m apart.

50 ft. Main Street from Valley View to Ryerson Avenue, Reeve, Leary and Ryerson Avenues north to Wanaque Road (now Oak Street), Valley View, High; Methodist Protestant Church, garages, Sloan Park island in the Pequannock.

sheet-4-1.description: The main part of sheet 4, at 100 feet to an inch, covers the eastern end of Bloomingdale from Ryerson Avenue to Van Dam Avenue and a stream beyond it, and from Main Street along the Pequannock River north to Poplar Street. It is a residential district laid out on a grid: Hennion Avenue, Ballston Avenue, Orchard and Hamilton Avenue run east and west between Union Avenue, Wallace Avenue, Park Avenue and Van Dam Avenue, with Wanaque Road running north-east from Union Avenue past Oak, Birch, Maple Avenue, Chestnut and Poplar. Several streets are marked not opened. Nearly all the buildings are one- and two-storey frame dwellings with outbuildings, a few concrete-block or brick ones, stores along Main Street and an automobile repair shop on Ballston Avenue. At the south-east corner Main Street meets a road crossing a concrete bridge, with Main Street in Riverdale beyond and a note referring to the map of Butler. The river along the southern edge has an island and carries the boundary between Bloomingdale and Riverdale and between Passaic and Morris Counties. Van Dam Avenue also carries the name Wanaque Avenue in brackets. A heavy line in the upper-left corner sets off an inset of Reeve Avenue north of Wanaque Road. The sheet has its own north point and scale.
notes: Wanaque Road is today Oak Street west of Union Avenue and Union Avenue north-east of it.
Hennion Avenue is today Henion Place, Ballston Avenue is Ballston Street, Hamilton Avenue is Hamilton Street, White Place is Whitehaven Place, Orchard is Orchard Street.
The short street named Oak, west of Wanaque Road, does not match today's Oak Street.

The sheet is drawn about 4 percent small and unevenly (fit RMSE about 4.3 m); the detected junction at Orchard and Wallace Avenue lay on the wrong lines and was excluded, and Ballston and Wallace was rejected.
Shared junction with sheet 3 at Wanaque Road and Ryerson Avenue placed about 6 m apart.

100 ft. Two parts. Part 1 (main): eastern Bloomingdale between Ryerson Avenue and Van Dam Avenue, Main Street to Poplar Street; Wanaque Road is now Oak Street (west of Union Avenue) and Union Avenue (north of it); Hennion Avenue is Henion Place, Ballston Avenue is Ballston Street, Hamilton Avenue is Hamilton Street, White Place is Whitehaven Place. Drawn about 4 percent small with an uneven fit (RMSE about 4.7 m). Part 2 (inset, upper left): Reeve Avenue north of Wanaque Road; placed from three hand-picked junctions along Oak Street (helmert).

sheet-4-2.description: An inset in the upper-left corner of sheet 4, set off by a heavy line and drawn at 100 feet to an inch with its own north point. It shows Reeve Avenue running north from Wanaque Road towards the hills above Bloomingdale, with Pleasant View Avenue joining at the corner, and the short stubs of Leary Avenue and Ryerson Avenue south of Wanaque Road, where the inset meets sheet 3. The area is thinly built: a row of frame dwellings and outbuildings along the west side of Reeve Avenue, a few dwellings near Wanaque Road and a large open block, numbered 129, bounded on the east by a high bank. Water pipes and a fire hydrant are drawn along Wanaque Road. The lettering along the eastern and southern borders notes that there is no exposure beyond.
notes: Wanaque Road is today Oak Street.
Placed from three hand-picked junctions along Oak Street (Reeve, Leary and Ryerson Avenues) as a helmert; the points lie on one line, so rotation rests on Oak Street alone.

sheet-5-1.description: The main part of sheet 5, at 100 feet to an inch, covers the western end of Bloomingdale along the Paterson and Hamburg Turnpike, from the edge of Butler to Bailey Avenue. The Turnpike crosses the sheet diagonally from the south-west to the north-east and meets Elizabeth, which continues over a steel bridge across the Pequannock River to Main Street and Laurel Street in Butler. North of the Turnpike a residential district is laid out along Vreeland Avenue, Ella, Elizabeth and Catherine, crossed by James, Hester, Mary, William and the diagonal Warren, with many lots still empty and widely scattered dwellings beyond the edges. In the north-east Ridge Road runs down past Avon Place, a short street given an arbitrary name, and Bailey Avenue runs north from the Turnpike. Industry lies by the river and the railroad: the Kitchell Wood Works on the Turnpike near Bailey Avenue, the Standard Coal and Lumber Co. building supplies yard by the Erie Railroad branch and its steel bridge in the south-west, and Star Light Park with its dance hall in the bend of the river. Buildings are mostly frame dwellings with a few stores. The river carries the county boundary between Passaic and Morris Counties. A heavy line sets off an inset in the lower right. The sheet has its own north point and scale.
notes: Ridge Road is today Star Lake Road.
Ella, William, Elizabeth, Catherine, Mary, Hester and Warren are today Ella, William, Elizabeth, Catherine, Mary, Hester and Warren Streets; James is James Avenue.
The railroad in the south-west is lettered E. R. R. N. Y. S. & W. R. R. (branch).
Works: Kitchell Wood Works; Standard Coal & Lumber Co., building supplies.

100 ft. Two parts. Part 1 (main): western Bloomingdale, Vreeland Avenue to Bailey Avenue along the Paterson and Hamburg Turnpike, Elizabeth, Catherine, Warren, Mary, William, Ella, Hester, James; Kitchell Wood Works, Standard Coal and Lumber Co., Star Light Park. Part 2 (inset, lower right): the Turnpike at Ridge Road (now Star Lake Road) and at Main and Old Road (now Fichter Street and Delazier Place); placed from one detected and one hand-picked junction (helmert).

sheet-5-2.description: An inset in the lower-right corner of sheet 5, set off by a heavy line and drawn at 100 feet to an inch with its own north point. It continues the Paterson and Hamburg Turnpike east of the main part of the sheet, along the north bank of the Pequannock River towards sheet 1. Ridge Road comes down from the north-west to meet the Turnpike, and further east the Turnpike divides: Old Road runs east along the upper side, and a road lettered Main comes down from the north to the fork. The ground between the Turnpike and the river is open with a steep bank, and a street marked not named runs south from the Turnpike in the south-west corner. Buildings are a scattering of frame dwellings and outbuildings along the Turnpike and Ridge Road. The county boundary between Passaic and Morris Counties follows the river, with a note referring to the map of Butler for the far bank.
notes: Ridge Road is today Star Lake Road; Old Road is today Delazier Place; the road lettered Main at the fork is today Fichter Street.

Placed from two points 93 m apart, the detected junction of the Turnpike and Ridge Road and a hand-picked junction of Main and Old Road (Fichter Street and Delazier Place), as a helmert; low confidence.
